gaps.hint: negative adjective needed (-ish): not appropriate for an adult
gaps.explanation: 'Childish' is negative (silly, immature); 'childlike' is positive (innocent). The embarrassment shows the negative sense.

gaps.sentence: Don't ___ your children — let them make their own mistakes (PROTECT).
gaps.hint: protect too much (over-); a base verb is needed
gaps.explanation: The prefix over- means excessively: overprotect means to protect too much. A base verb follows 'Don't'.

gaps.sentence: It is almost ___ to park in the city centre (POSSIBLE).
gaps.hint: negative adjective needed — parking is extremely difficult
gaps.explanation: The in- of 'possible' becomes im- before p: impossible. The context shows a negative meaning.

gaps.sentence: The training course will ___ you to work abroad (QUALIFY).
gaps.explanation: The suffix -ify forms the verb: qualify. A base verb follows 'will'.

gaps.sentence: She has been a loyal ___ (EMPLOY) of the firm for twenty years.
gaps.hint: person needed: someone who works for the firm
gaps.explanation: An employee works for a company; 'employment' is the uncountable state of having a job.

gaps.sentence: The thunderstorm was absolutely ___ , so the children hid under the blankets (TERRIFY).
gaps.hint: the storm causes the fear (-ing); note 'terrific' means excellent
gaps.explanation: The storm causes terror, so it is terrifying; the children felt terrified. 'Terrific' means excellent.
After 'an important' a noun is needed: discovery (note the change from -er to -y).

gaps.sentence: The old factory will be ___ into flats (MODERN).
gaps.hint: verb needed in the passive (-ise); past participle
gaps.explanation: The suffix -ise forms the verb: modernise. The passive 'will be' needs the past participle 'modernised'.
